newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dasa -Lagardere missile pact could change.
newsitem.headline: Dasa -Lagardere missile pact could change.

text.p: Daimler-Benz Aerospace AG said on Sunday it might rethink a portion of its cooperation with France's Lagardere, if Lagardere fails in its bid for defense electronics group Thomson-CSF.

In May Dasa and Lagardere agreed to join space activities and cooperate in missiles, but they may have to alter the missiles portion if Lagardere does not get the French government's 58 percent stake in Thomson-CSF, Dasa chief executive Manfred Bischoff said.
"Both companies intended to cooperate based on the purchase of Thomson-CSF," Bischoff said after a news conference at the Paris airshow.
"If Lagardere doesn't have Thomson, there is a smaller basis for coooperation on their side and we would have to see if the venture makes sense."
If the Thomson bid fails, Lagardere and Dasa could bring in a third partner into their missile actvities, or could consider restructuring their agreement.
Lagardere was expected to take a 30 percent share in Dasa's LFK GmbH missiles guidance business, with an option to increase that to 49 percent, Bischoff confirmed.
He did not rule out ending joint missiles activities, if the Thomson bid is unsuccessful. "That would have to be a possibility, if we have to discuss a new basis and cannot agree," Bischoff said.

The sale of Thomson-CSF, which is also sought by Alcatel Alsthom, was put into doubt by the arrival of France's new Socialist government, which opposed privatising national concerns in its election campaign.

Regardless of Thomson's fate, Dasa and Lagardere would continue their space cooperation, Bischoff said. They planned to combine Dasa's space operations with Mantra Marconi Space, a venture 51 percent owned by Lagardere and 49 percent owned by Britain's GEC.
